message.content:
Here’s a quick‑look at the **federal holidays that create “long weekends” in Canada for 2023**.  
(If you’re planning for a specific province, let me know – many provinces add extra holidays that also give you extra days off.)

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Long‑weekend span (including adjacent weekend days) |
|---------|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| New Year’s Day | Sunday Jan 1 | **Sat Dec 31 – Mon Jan 2** |
| Family Day (Alberta, Saskatchewan, etc.) | Monday Feb 20 | **Sat Feb 18 – Mon Feb 20** |
| Good Friday | Friday Apr 7 | **Fri Apr 7 – Sun Apr 9** |
| Victoria Day | Monday May 22 | **Sat May 20 – Mon May 22** |
| Canada Day | Saturday Jul 1 (observed Mon Jul 3) | **Sat Jul 1 – Mon Jul 3** |
| Labour Day | Monday Sep 4 | **Sat Sep 2 – Mon Sep 4** |
| Thanksgiving | Monday Oct 9 | **Sat Oct 7 – Mon Oct 9** |
| Remembrance Day | Saturday Nov 11 (observed Mon Nov 13) | **Sat Nov 11 – Mon Nov 13** |
| Christmas Day | Monday Dec 25 | **Sat Dec 23 – Mon Dec 25** |

> **Quick note:**  
> • Canada Day and Remembrance Day are observed on the following Monday if they fall on a weekend.  
> • Some provinces observe additional holidays (e.g., Civic Holiday on the first Monday in August, Family Day on the third Monday in February in Ontario, etc.).  

Feel free to let me know if you’d like the provincial variations or a more detailed calendar!
